fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the street entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point, especially at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so that fire apparatus and large emergency vehicles can travel the full length without obstruction.
• Maintain at least 14 feet of vertical clearance and 12 feet of horizontal clearance along the full length of the driveway.
• Post a visible sign or marker at the base of the driveway indicating that a second structure exists on the property so arriving responders know to account for both buildings.
• Mark the location of the detached structure from the driveway so responders can locate it without searching through vegetation.
• Trim dense vegetation along the sides of the driveway to maintain clear sightlines between the street and the main residence.
• Keep a clear path between the two structures so responders can move between them on foot without pushing through vegetation.
• Identify and maintain a flat, firm area near each structure where responders can stage equipment and personnel.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, stored equipment, and debris so the full length remains passable at all times.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and low branches that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls and foundation.
• Thin the tree cluster near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches from scattered trees near the structure so flames cannot climb from ground-level plants into the tree canopy.
• Clear brush from the area immediately surrounding the structure to open up space between the vegetation and the building.
• Mow or cut grass around the structure regularly, especially during dry periods, to reduce the amount of burnable material close to the house.
• Separate scattered shrubs near the structure so there are visible gaps between individual plants rather than a continuous bed of vegetation.
• Thin mixed vegetation on all sides of the structure to increase open space and reduce the amount of plant material that could carry fire toward the building.
• Trim overhanging branches and cut back shrubs along the full length of the driveway so vehicles, including fire trucks, can pass through without obstruction.
• Clear vegetation along driveway edges back far enough that a wide vehicle can travel the full length without contact with plants on either side.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from the brush area nearest the structure before dry season.
